name: hamming_weight_phasing_equal_angle_groups
precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz and ancilla_room; at least 4 non-Clifford Rz gates sharing one angle value (up to sign, modulo 2pi) whose front-frame Pauli axes pairwise commute; qubits <= 20 so the frozen whole-circuit check still runs
identity: Let P_1..P_k be pairwise commuting Paulis and apply exp(-i theta P_j / 2) for the SAME theta to all of them. Because they commute, the product is diag in a common basis: pick a Clifford C with C P_j C^dag = Z_{a_j} (or, if k exceeds the width, copy each parity onto a fresh clean ancilla a_j by CNOTs, which is what the implementation does: a_j holds the eigenvalue bit b_j of P_j). Then the product acts as exp(-i theta/2 * sum_j (-1)^{b_j}) = a phase e^{i theta (w - k/2)} where w = sum_j b_j is the Hamming weight of the k ancilla bits. Compute w into an m = ceil(log2(k+1))-bit register W by a tree of full adders, each full adder built from one Gidney and_compute gadget (4 T) plus CNOTs; apply rz(2^i * theta) on bit i of W for i = 0..m-1, together with a global-phase-only rz(-k theta/2) correction that is dropped; then uncompute the adder tree with and_uncompute (0 T, measurement + classically controlled CZ fix-up) and undo the parity copies. k equal-angle rotations are replaced by m = ceil(log2(k+1)) rotations of angles theta, 2theta, ..., 2^{m-1} theta plus (k - m) AND gadgets.
correctness: Commuting Paulis generate an abelian group, so the k exponentials can be reordered arbitrarily and simultaneously diagonalized; the parity copy b_j -> ancilla is the standard CNOT fan-in and is exact and reversible. On every computational-basis state of the diagonalized frame the applied phase is theta * (w - k/2) with w the exact Hamming weight, which is what the adder tree computes classically; identical phase for every branch, so invariant 2 (phase consistency) holds. and_compute/and_uncompute is Gidney's temporary-AND: exact, ancillas return to |0>, the measurement fix-up is a Clifford conditioned on the measured bit, so every branch realises the same unitary. Angle arithmetic 2^i theta is exact in the rotation angle (no snapping). Hence error_class = exact and nothing is drawn from the ledger.
trigger: Run v4.api.pauli.frames(ops) once. Bucket records by reduced |theta| (tolerance 1e-9) keeping the sign as a flag, discarding on_grid records. Inside a bucket, build the commutation graph on the record Paulis and take a maximal clique-by-greedy set that is also reorderable (every record in the set commutes with every rotation Pauli lying between the set's first and last positions, the same reorderability test pauli_frame_rotation_merge uses). Emit a match for each such set of size k >= 4, largest first, sets disjoint. On this circuit the buckets are the angle histogram: 15,15,15,15,14,10,10,10,10,10,6 and nine of size 4.
expected_effect: All 11238 of the 11364 T come from gridsynth on 204 off-grid rz at eps_rz = 4.9e-6 (~55 T each); the 126 explicit t/tdg are free of synthesis. The 204 rotations carry only 50 distinct angles. If the reorderable commuting fraction of each equal-angle bucket is ~60% of its size, roughly 125 of the 204 rotations fold into weight registers, leaving about 145 rotations (~55 T each = ~7975 T) plus about 80 AND gadgets at 4 T (= 320 T) plus the 126 explicit T, i.e. ~8420 T; with the full buckets usable it would be ~105 rotations + 99 ANDs = ~6300 T. Costs about 6 extra clean ancillas (8 -> ~14 qubits) and several hundred CNOTs, both of which are below T in the lexicographic cost order. This is the one lever neither pyzx (unitary rotation merging; these rotations are blocked, foldable_remaining = 0) nor DPF (unitary angle snapping) can reach, because it needs ancillas and measurement to convert angle MULTIPLICITY into binary-weighted arithmetic.
source: Hamming weight phasing: Kivlichan, Gidney, Berry, Wiebe, McClean, Sun, Jiang, Rubin, Fowler, Aspuru-Guzik, Neven, Babbush, 'Improved Fault-Tolerant Quantum Simulation of Condensed-Phase Correlated Electrons via Trotterization', Quantum 4, 296 (2020), Sec. 'Hamming weight phasing'; temporary-AND gadget: Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018)
